errors: Notational inconsistency, not a mathematical error: 𝔗_X is written 𝔗_{X,x} in (4). The 𝔗 and N groups depend only on ξ, so Q_X needs no x.
Q̃ ≃ P ∧^{M} Q̄ implicitly treats Q̄ (the closure in C) as an M_{g,ν}-set via M → Γ_{Q̄/Q}. This is correct but unstated.
No genuine mathematical errors. The contracted-product formalism for inner twists of normal subgroups is correct.

ideas.what: Path torsor (bitorsor) between geometric base points on the universal curve / moduli stack; identification of all π_1's at (X,x) as twists of standard ones by contracted product
ideas.modern_name: Étale fundamental groupoid; torsor of étale paths; base-point change via inner twisting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1); path torsors in arithmetic later emphasized by Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points') and Ihara
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. V (fundamental groupoid); Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower as a groupoid with many base points); 1983 letter to Faltings (anabelian context)

ideas.what: Arithmetic Teichmüller tower: diagram of exact sequences π̂_{g,ν} ⊂ 𝔊̂ ⊂ M_{g,ν}, with quotients 𝔗̂_{g,ν} and Γ_{Q̄/Q}; profinite mapping class group extended by the Galois group
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic mapping class group / outer Galois representation on π_1 of moduli stacks (Birman exact sequence, profinite version)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984); developed by Ihara, Nakamura, Matsumoto, Hain–Matsumoto, Boggi

ideas.what: Recovering Q̃ (the algebraic closure of Q in k) as a twist R ∧ Q̄ of the closure in C
ideas.modern_name: Galois torsor of embeddings / isomorphisms of algebraic closures

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine but careful set-up: torsor-of-paths bookkeeping expressing every arithmetic fundamental group attached to a pointed curve as a twist of the standard Teichmüller-tower groups. This is the standard groupoid formalism of SGA1 applied to M_{g,ν}. The interesting anabelian question (what P_{X,x} determines, and finiteness via finitely generated subfields) starts on the next page.
transcription_corrections: First line is likely 'La classe des chemins de x_0 (or ξ_0) à x définissent un torseur', i.e. paths from the reference point to the given point, not 'données de ρ à ξ'.
'(commutant à [?] M_{X,x})' is likely '(commutant à l'action de M_{X,x})' or similar, i.e. a left action commuting with the right one (bitorsor).
The fraktur group written 𝔖 / 𝔖̂_{g,ν} is the same 𝔊 / 𝔊̂_{g,ν} as on the previous page (π_1 of the geometric universal curve).
'soit déduit [?] du diagramme [?] analogue' is likely 'soit déduit du diagramme analogue pour (X_0,x_0)'.
'sur ses [?] filtrations [?] par' is likely 'et sur sa filtration par 𝔊̂_{g,ν}, π̂_{g,ν}'.
In (4) the 𝔊 line has a crossed-out marginal 'M_{X,x}'. The 𝔗 line's 'Q_X' appears in the image as 'Q_{X_0}'/'Q_X'; it should be Q_X as in (5).
